confirmed_findings.title: Unauthenticated Direct Access to Protected Master Vault via Public Media Proxy
confirmed_findings.description: Public media streaming endpoint at /api/media/[...path] permits traversal into the protected vault directory (public/media/vault/), exposing high-resolution raw master artwork scans without watermark or authentication.

exploit_scenario.impact: Unwatermarked high-value master art scans are downloaded directly, bypassing asset protection policies.

confirmed_findings.remediation: Explicitly block any request with segment starting with 'vault' and ensure targetFilePath does not resolve inside public/media/vault.

confirmed_findings.title: Missing Root Next.js Middleware Guard due to Filename Misconfiguration
confirmed_findings.description: The edge authentication proxy guard is named src/proxy.ts rather than src/middleware.ts. Next.js App Router ignores proxy.ts entirely, resulting in zero middleware execution on incoming requests.

exploit_scenario.impact: Route-level edge redirection is bypassed, relying solely on client-side or per-page guards.

evidence.vulnerable_code: export function proxy(request: NextRequest) { ... } export const config = { matcher: ['/admin/:path*'] };
evidence.proof_of_concept: Direct HTTP request to /admin bypasses edge filter when middleware.ts is absent.

confirmed_findings.remediation: Create src/middleware.ts exporting middleware() with route guards for /admin/:path* and /api/admin/:path*.

confirmed_findings.title: Arbitrary Outbound Email Relay via Unsanitized recipientEmails Parameter
confirmed_findings.description: The public contact/commission submission endpoint accepts client-supplied recipientEmails parameter, allowing an attacker to specify arbitrary recipient addresses and utilize the server as an open mail relay.

exploit_scenario.impact: Attacker uses the atelier SMTP server to send spam or phishing emails, harming domain reputation and risking IP blacklisting.

confirmed_findings.remediation: Do not accept arbitrary recipient emails from unauthenticated client requests; route all form inquiries solely to pre-configured administrative inboxes.

confirmed_findings.title: Missing Enterprise HTTP Security Headers
confirmed_findings.description: next.config.ts lacks HTTP security headers configuration, leaving responses without HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, or Permissions-Policy.

exploit_scenario.attack_vector: Clickjacking or MIME sniffing against visitor sessions.
exploit_scenario.impact: Vulnerability to clickjacking in iframes, MIME confusion, and lack of strict TLS enforcement.

evidence.vulnerable_code: const nextConfig: NextConfig = { output: 'standalone', ... } // No headers() defined

confirmed_findings.remediation: Add headers() function to next.config.ts specifying HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy.

confirmed_findings.title: Absence of Rate Limiting on Inbound Lead & Registration Endpoints
confirmed_findings.description: Public endpoints /api/events/register, /api/forms/submit, and /api/leads/submit lack rate limiting, allowing automated scripts to flood the database with fake registrations and exhaust event ticket capacity.

exploit_scenario.impact: Denial of service for legitimate event attendees, database row flooding, and SMTP queue starvation.

evidence.vulnerable_code: export async function POST(request: NextRequest) { // No rate check }
evidence.proof_of_concept: for i in {1..1000}; do curl -X POST /api/events/register ...; done

confirmed_findings.remediation: Implement an IP-based sliding window rate limiter (e.g. 5 req/min) using Cloudflare CF-Connecting-IP header.

confirmed_findings.title: Missing Cross-Origin Request Validation (CSRF/CORS) on State-Mutating APIs
confirmed_findings.description: State-mutating endpoints do not enforce Origin / Referer validation against allowed domains, permitting cross-site forged POST submissions.

exploit_scenario.attack_vector: Cross-site submission from malicious external origin.
exploit_scenario.impact: Automated submission of inquiries on behalf of the victim.

evidence.vulnerable_code: No origin header verification performed prior to mutation.

confirmed_findings.remediation: Enforce Origin validation in middleware or API routes against configured trusted origins.

confirmed_findings.title: Insecure TLS Certificate Verification in Outbound SMTP Transport
confirmed_findings.description: Nodemailer transport configuration explicitly sets rejectUnauthorized: false, disabling TLS certificate chain verification during SMTP transmission.

exploit_scenario.attack_vector: Man-in-the-middle attack on upstream SMTP traffic.
exploit_scenario.impact: Interception or tampering of lead contact details and emails.

evidence.proof_of_concept: Nodemailer accepts self-signed or fraudulent upstream certificates.

confirmed_findings.remediation: Remove rejectUnauthorized: false and enforce standard TLS certificate verification.

coverage_notes: Full audit covering App Router pages, API endpoints, media pipelines, authentication, and Docker build configuration.
